packageRules.description: Our packages are libraries. The >= floors in [project.dependencies] are a compatibility contract with downstream users, so Renovate only refreshes uv.lock and never raises a floor. Floors are raised by hand, when the code starts relying on a newer API.
build-system.requires is not recorded in uv.lock, so update-lockfile would freeze the build backend forever. Widen the bound instead.
One pull request per repository for every non-major Python update.
One pull request per repository for GitHub Actions. Digests stay pinned and the trailing # vX.Y.Z comment is kept in sync.
One pull request per repository for pre-commit hook revisions.
The python-scim packages are ours, so their new releases skip the cooldown meant for third-party releases, as uv's exclude-newer-package does in each project.
This preset is ours, so its new tags skip the cooldown meant for third-party releases. Minor and major versions of the preset are adopted through a reviewed pull request in each repository.
Patch versions of the preset are automerged. Only administrators can push the tags of this repository.

uv builds the releases with its bundled backend only when its version matches the uv_build range of build-system.requires, so the uv of setup-uv, the uv container image and that range move together in one pull request.
Major updates are never grouped and never automerged: each one gets its own pull request and a human review.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Weekly full refresh of uv.lock, which is the only way transitive dependencies ever move.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes bypass the weekly schedule and the 14 day cooldown, and always wait for a human.
